newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's stubborn jobless rate falls slightly.
newsitem.headline: Canada's stubborn jobless rate falls slightly.

text.p: Canada's stubbornly high unemployment rate slipped slightly in May to 9.5 percent from 9.6 percent in April -- almost twice the U.S. jobless rate of 4.8 percent in May, Statistics Canada reported on Friday.
But job creation was stronger than expected, with 61,300 new jobs in May. Full-time employment rose by 70,300 in May, the government statistics agency said.

"How can anyone be anything but supremely bullish on the Canadian economy at a time when more than 140,000...full-time jobs have been created over the past three months," brokerage Nesbitt Burns wrote in its morning commentary.
The unemployment rate stayed high despite the strong job creation numbers, mainly because the labor force grew by 50,500 people as the number of jobs grew, Statistics Canada said.
The picture was not so rosy for youth and part-time workers, with part-time jobs down by 9,000 in May.
The unemployment rate among people aged 15 to 24 was 17.2 percent in May, up 0.2 percentage points from April and up 1.7 points from a year ago, Statistics Canada said.
"Job prospects for youths remain poor," the agency said.

Unemployment dropped significantly in Ontario -- Canada's richest and most populous province -- to 8.5 percent from 9 percent. But in Canada's poorest province, Newfoundland, the unemployment rate jumped 1.4 points to 20.5 percent.
The jobless rate in Canada has hovered between 9 and 10 percent since mid-1994, although the number of jobs in the country has risen steadily over that time.
